stem.text: Genetic engineering may often involve the transfer of a gene into an organism.
The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) can be used to produce many copies of a gene for transfer.
Describe and explain the steps involved in PCR.

4 (so that) primers, anneal / bind, (ss)DNA / complementary bases ;

explanation.text: PCR repeats denaturation, primer annealing and extension. In the idealised calculation the target doubles each cycle, so n cycles from one copy give 2 to the power n copies.

reasoningChain: Identify the role of primers, nucleotides and thermostable polymerase.
Trace the repeated stages or apply the doubling calculation.

inferredMistakes.text: Using twice the number of cycles as the number of DNA copies

stem.text: Some species of Anopheles mosquitoes, such as Anopheles stephensi, transmit malaria. Scientists have created genetically engineered A. stephensi mosquitoes in an attempt to reduce the spread of malaria.
A gene called tTav was constructed by scientists and transferred into the eggs of A. stephensi.

items: tTav consists of DNA sequences from a bacterium, Escherichia coli, and herpes simplex virus, which is a DNA virus.
The gene codes for tTav protein, which stops the expression of genes that are essential to mosquito development.
Genetically engineered A. stephensi do not survive beyond the larval stage and therefore do not develop into adults.
A chemical called tetracycline can stop the action of the tTav protein.

stem.text: Male genetically engineered A. stephensi were released into the wild to breed with females. Their offspring had the tTav gene.
Describe how the tTav gene could have been synthesised and transferred into the eggs of A. stephensi.

markScheme.instruction: any four from: bacteria = E.coli and virus = herpes simplex throughout

points.text: 1 extract / isolate / cut, DNA (sequences) using restriction enzyme or make DNA (sequences) using mRNA using reverse transcriptase or make DNA (sequences) using nucleotides ;
2 use DNA ligase to join together (the two sequences of) DNA (of bacteria and virus) ;
4 add, tTav / recombinant DNA / gene, to, vector / virus / liposome ;
5 infect egg with virus or (micro)injection into egg ; A gene gun / DNA gun
6 virus adds, tTav / recombinant DNA / gene, into genome (of egg / A. stephensi) ;

explanation.text: A coding sequence can be obtained from donor DNA, mature mRNA via reverse transcription, or chemical synthesis. Mature mRNA has already had introns removed in eukaryotes.

reasoningChain: Choose the appropriate source of the coding sequence.
Explain why that source suits the recipient or desired sequence.

inferredMistakes.text: Transferring intron-containing eukaryotic DNA into bacteria without considering RNA processing

explanation.text: Structural genes encode functional products, while regulatory genes encode products that control expression of other genes. Induction changes expression rather than changing the DNA sequence.
